title: verification-gate.config.json
description: Per-project configuration for the verification-gate stage machine. Lives in the project root; the gates themselves stay framework-agnostic and read everything project-specific from here.

baselineDir.description: Directory holding frozen baselines and the validity report. Commit it — a baseline that is not versioned is not frozen.

stateDir.description: Where state.json and per-gate result JSON are written. Gitignore this.

freshness.description: Fixture-freshness gating. Checked once before any gate runs, if any staged gate sets requiresBaseline.

required.description: When false, a missing validity report is tolerated. Only sensible for gates that compare nothing captured.

stages.description: Gate ids in execution order. Every entry must have a matching key under "gates".

gates.description: Gate id to configuration. Resolution order: the gate's own "script" path wins if set (an explicit override should beat a convention), otherwise scripts/gates/gate-<id>.mjs, then scripts/modules/gate-<id>.mjs.

required.description: When true, a non-zero exit halts the chain. When false, the chain reports and continues.

requiresBaseline.description: Whether this gate reads a frozen baseline, and therefore whether the chain must validate fixture freshness before starting.

script.description: Path to a custom gate script, relative to the project root. Overrides the built-in lookup.

command.description: unit, flaky: shell command that runs the suite.

format.description: unit, flaky: how to read the runner's output.

parser.description: unit, flaky: with format "custom", path to an .mjs exporting parse(stdout, stderr) -> [{ name, status }].

resultsFile.description: unit, flaky: read results from this file instead of stdout. Its absence is treated as a runner that did not complete.

quarantine.description: unit: specs listed here report but never block. Each entry needs a spec and a reason.

minObserved.description: Fewest results a healthy run produces. Below this the gate is BLOCKED, not passed. Set it deliberately — the default of 1 only catches a total crash.

shrinkTolerance.description: Fraction the observed count may fall below the baseline count before the run is treated as broken rather than smaller.

runs.description: flaky: repeated trials used to separate flaky from broken.

captureCommand.description: integration, visual: project-owned command that produces the fresh capture.

captureOutput.description: integration, visual: NDJSON file the capture command writes.

key.description: integration, visual: fields identifying a record across captures.

compare.description: integration, visual: fields diffed on records the baseline covers. An empty list is rejected — it would pass trivially.

classify.description: integration, visual: rules moving a confirmed-cause finding from blocking to reported. Every rule needs a reason; rules without one are rejected.

reason.description: The confirmed root cause. This is printed next to the finding.

when.description: Finding field to regex. All must match.

scope.description: secrets: scan everything matching include, or only files changed against baseRef.

include.description: secrets: globs to scan. Matching zero files is BLOCKED, not clean.

debugGlobs.description: secrets: subset also checked for debugger and stray console statements. Keep CLI entry points out of it.

patterns.description: secrets: extra patterns beyond the built-ins.

allowlist.description: secrets: rule ids demoted to reported. Prefer an inline verification-gate:allow-secret comment on the specific line.

baseRef.description: git ref to diff against. The defaults differ by gate on purpose: contract uses HEAD~1 (what the last commit changed), secrets with scope "changed" uses HEAD (what you are about to commit, which is the thing worth scanning before it lands).

sourceGlobs.description: contract: files whose change demands a test change.

testGlobs.description: contract: files that count as tests.

requiredSpecs.description: contract: the strong form. Names the specific spec a kind of source change must be covered by, so touching an unrelated test cannot satisfy the rule.

spec.description: Exact spec path that must also have changed.
